docs.title: Spring AI ACP Harness Client Reference
docs.text:
Spring AI ACP Harness Client (SAAHC, pronounced "sock") drives any Agent Client Protocol coding agent (Goose, Codex, OpenCode, or any of the agents in the ACP registry) from a Spring Boot application, behind one API and one configuration model.

A harness is the coding agent runtime you drive, such as Goose, Codex or OpenCode. SAAHC creates no agent of its own: it configures a harness, launches or attaches to it, and talks to it over ACP. So its types say harness: AcpHarnessClient is your application's client, AcpHarnessSession a session the harness holds, AcpHarnessEvent what it streamed back. ACP calls the two ends of the connection the client and the agent, and this documentation keeps that word for the running program.

SAAHC relates to coding agents the way Spring Data relates to databases:

  • application code talks to one abstraction, AcpHarnessClient;
  • configuration carries options that work on every agent, plus a per-agent escape hatch;
  • the agent behind it is chosen by one property, spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime.
application.yaml
spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        runtime: goose        # or codex, opencode, a registry id
        model: gpt-5.6-terra  # a request, not an assignment

String answer = acpHarnessClient.prompt()
        .session("review-123")
        .user("Inspect this change")
        .call()
        .content();

The agent itself is a separate process: SAAHC launches it (or attaches to it), speaks ACP to it over stdio or WebSocket, supervises it, and turns what it streams back into typed Java events. Around that conversation, SAAHC configures the things that make an agent yours:

Concern What it gives the agent Configured by Runtime Which agent runs spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime and a runtime starter (Agent Runtimes) Model Which LLM it thinks with, and where it reaches it spring.ai.acp.harness.model, spring.ai.acp.harness.provider.* (Models and Providers) MCP servers Tools: your APIs, databases, internal services spring.ai.acp.harness.mcp-servers (MCP Servers) Skills Procedures it loads when a task calls for them spring.ai.acp.harness.skills (Skills) Instructions A standing system prompt, always in context AGENTS.md in the workspace (Agent Instructions) Permissions Which tool calls it may make without a human spring.ai.acp.harness.permissions, spring.ai.acp.harness.mode (Permissions)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
---
config:
  flowchart:
    wrappingWidth: 640
---
flowchart TD
    app["<b>Your application</b><br/>AcpHarnessClient · AcpHarnessSessions · AcpChatModel (Spring AI) · optional HTTP endpoint"]
    core["<b>spring-ai-acp-harness-client</b><br/>connection pool · session registry · config negotiation · permission policy<br/>MCP credential proxy · skill installer · workspace jail · observations"]
    subgraph adapters["Runtime adapters"]
        direction LR
        goose["<b>goose</b><br/>stdio or WebSocket"]
        codex["<b>codex</b><br/>codex-acp via npx"]
        opencode["<b>opencode</b><br/>stdio"]
        registry["<b>registry</b><br/>any published agent"]
        goose ~~~ codex ~~~ opencode ~~~ registry
    end
    agent["<b>Agent process</b><br/>reads AGENTS.md and .agents/skills/ from the workspace, calls MCP servers, calls the model"]
    app --> core
    core -- "AcpHarnessRuntime SPI" --> adapters
    adapters -- "ACP v1 (com.agentclientprotocol:acp-core)" --> agent

Figure 1. Application code depends only on the top layer. Vendor knowledge lives only in the runtime adapters.

docs.title: Three tiers of configuration
docs.text:
ACP standardizes the conversation, not the provisioning. So each property belongs to one of three tiers, and the tier tells you how portable it is:

Tier Where Guarantee Portable spring.ai.acp.harness.* Honoured by every runtime: workspace, mcp-servers, skills, permissions, timeout, provider credentials. Negotiated spring.ai.acp.harness.model, .mode, .provider.id A request. Resolved against the options the agent advertises; on-unsupported decides what happens when it cannot be honoured. Runtime-specific spring.ai.acp.harness.runtimes.<id>.* Passed to that one adapter untouched and ignored by every other, so blocks for several runtimes can sit side by side.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Artifact Contents spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-goose Starter plus the Goose adapter spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-codex Starter plus the Codex adapter (@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp) spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-opencode Starter plus the OpenCode adapter spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-registry Starter plus the registry runtime: any agent the ACP registry publishes spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter Core and auto-configuration with no agent (for bringing your own AcpHarnessRuntime) spring-ai-acp-harness-client The library itself, without Spring Boot: AcpHarnessClient, sessions, configuration, MCP proxy, workspace spring-ai-acp-harness-client-chatmodel AcpChatModel: the agent as a Spring AI ChatModel spring-ai-acp-harness-client-mcp-oauth Per-user OAuth sign-in to MCP servers (Spring Security) spring-ai-acp-harness-client-console A terminal chat over the agent, for prototyping it (JLine); answers policy: ask spring-ai-acp-harness-client-test ScriptedAcpAgent, AcpHarnessProbe, and the AcpHarnessRuntimeContract conformance suite

The starters bring in spring-ai-acp-harness-client, spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-autoconfigure and the matching spring-ai-acp-harness-client-runtime-* adapter, so applications rarely name those directly.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Spring AI ACP Harness Client are documented here. The project follows Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A supervised agent whose start failed, or whose WebSocket transport could not be constructed, left the supervisor, transport or log watcher it had created behind. AcpHarnessClientFactory now closes what it created before rethrowing, and a supervisor closes the client it uses for health probes.
  • The WebSocket transport now waits for its close frame to be sent before shutting its HttpClient down, and shuts the executor down with it, so the agent sees a normal closure rather than a reset. Its client and executors are released once however the socket ended, including when the agent closed it first — the usual way a restarted agent's connection ends. The MCP loopback proxy closes its HttpClient on close too.
  • The endpoint model catalogue now uses one HttpClient for the JVM instead of one per agent connection, so reconnecting no longer accumulates selector threads and connection pools.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • The project now goes by SAAHC (pronounced "sock") for short. The documentation introduces it as "Spring AI ACP Harness Client (SAAHC)" and uses it after that. Nothing technical is renamed: artifacts, packages, properties and types keep their names.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• ACP Java SDK 0.80.0 (#28). An application that uses the SDK's own types through this library meets its breaking changes; its CHANGELOG has a migration for each. The ones most likely to show:
  • StopReason, ToolCallStatus, PermissionOptionKind, PlanEntryStatus, PlanEntryPriority and Role are open value records rather than enums, so a newer agent's value no longer fails to read. Compare them with equals and switch on value(). Observation tags, AcpController's stopReason and AcpChatModel's finish reason keep their upper-case spellings (END_TURN).
  • ToolCall, ToolCallUpdate and their notification gain a name component, and the short session-update constructors no longer take the discriminator.
  • A select option's values are SessionConfigSelectOptions, flat or grouped; read them with allOptions(). Grouped options are matched like flat ones.
  • The legacy models state and session/set_model are no longer used. They never became stable ACP, and the SDK no longer models them. Mechanism.SESSION_MODEL is removed. goose, Codex and OpenCode all offer the model as a config option, which is unchanged; an agent that offers models only the old way now gets on-unsupported handling for model. ScriptedAcpAgent.Builder.models(...) still advertises the old state, for testing exactly that.
  • providers/set sends the provider as providerId, the schema's name for it and the one Codex reads. The SDK used to send id.
  • A turn that times out, or whose stream is cancelled, and whose agent has not answered session/cancel within 5 seconds, also sends $/cancel_request for its session/prompt, from the SDK. goose and OpenCode ignore it.
  • session/close is sent only to an agent that advertises sessionCapabilities.close, which the SDK now enforces. goose and OpenCode do.
  • A config option the SDK cannot read at all, such as a select mixing options and groups, now fails session/new rather than being skipped. An option of a type it does not know is still kept, as UnknownSessionConfigOption.
  • Removed SessionConfigRecorder and SessionUpdateDecoder, which worked around SDK gaps that 0.80.0 closes, and the recorder parameter of DefaultAcpHarnessClient and DefaultAcpHarnessSessions. session/load and session/resume are no longer serialized.
  • AcpHarnessTurn now releases the session's turn permit itself, when the agent is done with the session, so a caller of AcpHarnessTurn.prompt acquires it and no longer releases it.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A supervised agent (serve.transport: websocket) that failed to become ready was restarted by its own exit. After a start that failed, the supervisor went on spawning the agent in the background, although the caller had been told it did not start. A restart that failed scheduled two more, and the second spawned an agent beside the first that the application's shutdown never stopped. Only an agent that became ready and then exits is now restarted, once. Reported, with a proposed fix and its test, by @zjxzjw in #31.
  • A per-turn timeout longer than spring.ai.acp.harness.timeout was ignored: the SDK bounded session/prompt by the client-wide timeout, so the turn failed at that one. The SDK no longer bounds prompts, so the turn's own timeout applies (#25).
  • A turn that timed out left its session/prompt in the SDK's table of pending requests until the agent answered it, so an agent that hung and ignored session/cancel grew that table by one entry per timed-out turn. The SDK now forgets a request its caller gave up on.
  • A turn that exceeded timeout ended with Failed but never sent session/cancel, so the agent kept working on the prompt, spending tokens on a result nobody received. A timed-out turn now sends session/cancel, as a cancelled stream already did (#20).
  • The next turn on a session could overlap one that was cancelled or timed out. The session was handed on as soon as session/cancel was sent, but ACP lets the agent keep sending until it answers the cancelled prompt, and goose, Codex and OpenCode all do: a usage_update or session_info_update a few milliseconds later, which the next turn received as its own. The agent could also get the next prompt while still finishing the last. The session now stays busy until the agent answers the cancelled prompt, or for 5 seconds if it never does, and what it sends meanwhile is dropped. The caller still hears that the turn ended at once (#27).
  • A permission request still open when its turn was cancelled or timed out was never answered, as ACP requires, and with policy: ask the person went on being asked. If they answered, their choice went to the agent for a turn that had already ended. The client now answers such a request cancelled at once, answers any that arrive while the agent winds down the same way, and interrupts the PermissionPrompt still asking; a later answer is discarded. goose 1.57 was seen to ignore a late answer, so nothing ran (#26).

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • PromptSpec.waitIfBusy(Duration) sets how long a turn waits for a named session that is still running an earlier turn, before failing with the new AcpHarnessSessionBusyException. Duration.ZERO fails at once; the default is still the turn's timeout. A session is now free again before its caller hears that a turn ended, so a caller that goes straight on to the next turn never finds it busy.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: Java packages move from org.springaicommunity.acp.* to org.springaicommunity.acp.harness.*, to match the artifacts and the properties. Update your imports, and any logging.level.org.springaicommunity.acp setting, which otherwise stops matching without an error. The JDBC schema for MCP OAuth moves with them, to org/springaicommunity/acp/harness/mcp/oauth/acp-mcp-oauth-schema.sql.
  • Breaking: every AcpAgent… type becomes AcpHarness…, starting with AcpAgentClient, which becomes AcpHarnessClient (with DefaultAcpHarnessClient, AcpHarnessClientPool, AcpHarnessClientFactory and AcpHarnessClientException, and the bean acpAgentClient becomes acpHarnessClient). This library creates no agent: it configures an existing agent harness such as Goose, Codex or OpenCode, launches or attaches to it, and talks to it over ACP, so the types describe the harness and now say so, as the project, its artifacts, its packages and its spring.ai.acp.harness.* properties already did. ACP itself calls the far end of the connection the agent, and the documentation keeps that word for the running program. Hence AcpHarnessRuntime, AcpHarnessRuntimeProvider, AcpHarnessLaunchSpec, AcpHarnessEnvironment, AcpHarnessNotice, AcpHarnessSession, AcpHarnessSessions, AcpHarnessTurn, AcpHarnessEvent, AcpHarnessEventMapper, AcpHarnessInfo, AcpHarnessSettings, AcpHarnessOptions, AcpHarnessObservations, AcpHarnessTurnObservationContext, AcpHarnessExecutor, AcpHarnessLogWatcher, AcpHarnessProcessSupervisor, UnsupportedAcpHarnessOperationException, UnsupportedAcpHarnessOptionException, the nested AcpHarnessClient.AcpHarnessResponse and AcpHarnessStream, the registry runtime's AcpHarnessRegistry, AcpHarnessInstaller and AcpHarnessInstallException, the Boot AcpHarnessConfigDataLoader, AcpHarnessConfigDataLocationResolver and AcpHarnessConfigDataResource (formerly AcpAgentsConfigData…, with an s), and the test kit's AcpHarnessRuntimeContract and AcpHarnessProbe. AcpHarnessClient.agentInfo() becomes harnessInfo(), on the pool too. The beans acpAgentSettings, acpAgentRegistry, acpAgentInstaller, acpAgentObservations and acpAgentExecutor follow as acpHarness…, and the adapter beans an application overrides by name are now gooseHarnessRuntime, codexHarnessRuntime, openCodeHarnessRuntime and registryHarnessRuntimeProvider instead of …AgentRuntime…. The rule is mechanical, so replacing each AcpAgent or AcpAgents type-name prefix with AcpHarness migrates an application, and the compiler finds every site; a bean overridden by its old name is the one thing it cannot catch, so check those four by hand. Unchanged: packages, properties, metric names, and the test doubles that play the ACP agent role on the wire, ScriptedAcpAgent and LiveAcpAgents, since those are agents in the protocol's sense.
  • Breaking: the observations and their tags are named the way Spring AI names its own, so a dashboard or alert on the old names must be updated. The two observations are spring.ai.acp.harness.turn and spring.ai.acp.harness.tool.call (were acp.turn and acp.tool.call); the model tag is the OpenTelemetry gen_ai.response.model (was acp.model), the key Spring AI's chat models carry, so one breakdown by model covers both; every other key keeps its suffix under spring.ai.acp.harness. instead of acp. (.runtime, .session.kind, .outcome, .session.name, .context.used, .context.size, .cost, .tool.kind, .tool.status, .tool.title, .tool.id); and both observations gain Spring AI's spring.ai.kind tag, acp_harness_turn or acp_harness_tool_call. The outcome deliberately stays a single-valued tag of our own rather than gen_ai.response.finish_reasons, which Spring AI records as a high-cardinality list on the span. The bare acp. root was no library's to claim: ACP itself defines no telemetry names, and any other ACP library could have used the same ones. The AcpChatModel response metadata keys follow, and now spell the same thing the same way as the turn span: acp.runtime, acp.session, acp.context.used and acp.context.size become spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime, .session.name, .context.used and .context.size; acp.cost.amount and acp.cost.currency keep their typed split as .cost.amount and .cost.currency. An absent model is tagged none, Spring AI's spelling on that key, where it was unknown. For a custom ObservationConvention, the key constants are unchanged in meaning: the new spring.ai.kind constant is SPRING_AI_KIND on both low-cardinality enums, and ToolCallLowCardinalityKeys.KIND is still the ACP tool kind.
  • Breaking: configuration properties move from spring.acp.* to spring.ai.acp.harness.*, and environment variables from SPRING_ACP_* to SPRING_AI_ACP_HARNESS_*. The old root is shared with acp-autoconfig (spring.acp.client.*, spring.acp.agent.*), and the new one follows the spring.ai.* convention of the Spring AI Community projects. Update your configuration: the old keys are no longer read, and nothing reports them, so a spring.acp.*.enabled=false stops taking effect. The acp: config import prefix, metric names and Java packages are unchanged.
  • Breaking: the API no longer returns or accepts java.util.Optional. A value that may be absent is now a plain reference annotated with JSpecify's @Nullable, as Spring Framework 7 and Spring AI do, so client.session(name), client.harnessInfo(), sessions().find(name), SessionConfiguration.applied(option), AcpHarnessSession.principal(), RuntimeOptions.text(path) and the find* accessors of ProviderSpec and AcpHarnessSettings return null for "none". The SPI follows: AcpHarnessRuntime.authMethod, toolNameOf, planOf, logDirectory and noticeOf, AcpHarnessRuntimeProvider.forId, McpCredentialsProvider.credentialsFor, McpCredentials.upstream, ModelCatalog.modelsOf, SessionPrincipalResolver.current, PermissionPrompt.ask and both PermissionPolicy.decide methods return null instead of empty, and decide and PermissionQuestion take a nullable tool name. AcpHarnessOptions drops its find* methods, since its record accessors already say the same thing; StoredSession likewise drops findCwd, findTitle and findUpdatedAt, and ProviderSpec drops findBaseUrl. AcpHarnessEvent.UsageUpdated.contextFraction() returns a Double or null instead of an OptionalDouble. Replace .isPresent() with a null check and .orElse(x) with a conditional to migrate; the compiler finds every call site, since the types changed.
  • Every package of a published module is @NullMarked, so a reference is non-null unless it says @Nullable, and the build enforces that with NullAway: main code that passes, returns or stores a possibly-null value where a non-null one is declared no longer compiles. Nothing changes for a caller, except that a @Nullable on this API is now something the compiler checked rather than a comment. A few signatures gained a @Nullable the behaviour already implied, such as AcpHarnessExecutor.getVersion(), SkillFetcher.Fetched.revision(), McpServerSpec.Http.url(), AcpHarnessLaunchSpec.WebSocket.process() and the optional components of SkillSpec.Git and AcpController's request and response records; SecretRedactor.redact no longer accepts null. A few behaviours changed where a null used to flow on: SessionConfiguration.of(option) returns a NOT_REQUESTED resolution instead of null for an option the configuration never mentioned; a registry entry with no id, package, archive or command is skipped when the catalogue is parsed instead of failing at launch, and a registry agent with no distribution fails at launch with a message; a stored MCP OAuth client registration missing a required field fails with a message naming it; and an auth: oauth server declared without a url is refused when the credentials provider is built rather than when the first user's session opens. For a contributor, .mvn/jvm.config now opens the javac internals Error Prone needs, and spring-boot-configuration-processor is named on the compiler's processor path.
  • Breaking: the core library is now the artifact spring-ai-acp-harness-client, dropping the -core suffix, the Spring AI ChatModel adapter is spring-ai-acp-harness-client-chatmodel instead of -ai, and the parent POM is published as spring-ai-acp-harness-client-parent, so each name says what it is. Applications use a starter and rarely name the core artifact; one that names either changes the artifact id. Java packages are unchanged. The modules are also grouped into runtimes/, auto-configurations/, starters/ and integrations/ folders in the repository, which changes no artifact id.
  • Releases are published to Maven Central, and snapshots to the Maven Central snapshot repository. Versions up to 0.5.0 remain in the Artifact Registry repository.
  • The reference documentation moved from a single docs/user-guide.html to a versioned MkDocs site, published to GitHub Pages from docs/.
  • Breaking: AcpController's handlers return Mono or Flux, all but health, so that no request blocks a Netty event-loop thread. Requests over HTTP are unaffected; an application that calls the controller's methods directly subscribes to what they return.
  • Breaking: GET {path}/sessions on the HTTP endpoint returns [{"name", "sessionId", "title", "updatedAt"}], naming each of the caller's open sessions the way the caller did, so it can be continued or closed, instead of the agent's stored sessions. It no longer needs the agent to implement session/list (no more 501), asks the agent nothing when the caller has nothing open, and lists every open session, including one the agent has not saved yet or that runs in another process of the pool.
  • The HTTP endpoint answers a request for a named session that is still running an earlier turn with a 409 at once, instead of waiting for it for up to the request's timeout and then returning a 502. Waiting held a thread on the scheduler that also answers agents' permission and workspace requests, so one caller sending overlapping turns to one session could stall every other user's agent.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A new session that failed while being configured, such as an unsupported model with on-unsupported: fail, stayed open on the agent until session-ttl, with its MCP route still live. In a pool these sessions used up capacity, so later turns were refused with a "holding its maximum" error instead of reporting the real failure. A session that was already open is kept, so a bad per-turn override does not end a conversation. The same applied to a session attached with sessions().load or resume, which stayed loaded on the agent; it is now closed there too.
  • A session/new the agent answered after the caller stopped waiting, as when a cancelled turn interrupts its thread, named a session nothing could close; it is now closed when the answer arrives. A session/new not answered within timeout now fails with an AcpHarnessClientException instead of an IllegalStateException; an answer after that is dropped by the ACP SDK, so a session created that late still stays on the agent.
  • Subscribing twice to one throwaway AcpHarnessStream now runs two sessions. They used to share one, so the first to finish could close it under the other.
  • A closed AcpHarnessClientPool would start new agents on request, and a connection still being built when the pool closed was never closed. A closed pool now refuses work with an AcpHarnessClientException, and a connection that finishes building after the close is closed at once. Closing does not interrupt or wait for a connect in progress.
  • The HTTP endpoint blocked on the Netty event loop, so on a real server /prompt, /stream and listing sessions failed with a 500, and closing a session never reached the agent. It now runs turns without holding a thread.
  • The HTTP endpoint gave sessions no owner, so any caller could continue or close another user's session by naming it, and GET {path}/sessions listed everyone's. Session names are now scoped to the caller, and listing returns only the caller's open sessions. Names are limited to 109 characters, and the endpoint can no longer reach a session the application opened under the same name. On OpenCode, spring.ai.acp.harness.pool.max-processes now limits how many endpoint users can hold sessions.
  • /stream ended normally when a turn failed. It now returns a 502, or aborts the connection if text was already sent.
  • An invalid session name on the HTTP endpoint returned a 500, after the pool had assigned the name to a process. It is now a 400 before anything else happens.
  • A full pool is reported by the new AcpHarnessCapacityException, which the HTTP endpoint returns as a 503 instead of a 502 or 500.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Renamed from Spring AI ACP to Spring AI ACP Harness Client, ahead of moving to the Spring AI Community organisation. Every artifact moves from spring-ai-acp-* to spring-ai-acp-harness-client-* (for example spring-ai-acp-boot-starter-goose becomes spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-goose) under the same org.springaicommunity groupId; update your dependencies. Java packages (org.springaicommunity.acp.*) and configuration properties (spring.acp.*) are unchanged.
  • The live-test switches follow the new name: -Dspring-ai-acp-harness-client.test.live=true, -Dspring-ai-acp-harness-client.test.<runtimeId>.model and -Dspring-ai-acp-harness-client.test.registry.live=true.
  • The agent now sees the client as spring-ai-acp-harness-client in ACP initialize, as does an MCP authorization server registering it when spring.application.name is unset. State kept on disk keeps the former name so an upgrade finds it: the registry cache (~/.spring-ai-acp/agents), the .spring-ai-acp-skill marker, and the MCP sign-in file of an application without a spring.application.name. Such an application's console does take the new name, for its title and for its input history, which therefore starts afresh.
  • Every type named for the agent now says AcpAgent, so that it no longer reads as one of Spring AI's own agent types beside it: AgentClient becomes AcpAgentClient (and its nested AgentResponse and AgentStream, AcpAgentResponse and AcpAgentStream), AgentSession/AgentSessions become AcpAgentSession/AcpAgentSessions, AgentEvent becomes AcpAgentEvent, and likewise AcpAgentOptions, AcpAgentSettings, AcpAgentInfo, AcpAgentNotice, AcpAgentExecutor, AcpAgentClientException, UnsupportedAcpAgentOperationException and UnsupportedAcpAgentOptionException. The adapter SPI follows (AcpAgentRuntime, AcpAgentRuntimeProvider, AcpAgentLaunchSpec, AcpAgentEnvironment), as does the test kit (AcpAgentRuntimeContract, AcpAgentProbe, ScriptedAcpAgent, LiveAcpAgents) and every internal type. The rule is mechanical, so replacing each \bAgent…\b type name with its AcpAgent… spelling migrates an application; packages, bean names, configuration properties and the standalone configuration file are unchanged. Two exceptions: the transport for a supervised served agent, WebSocketAgentTransport, becomes SupervisedWebSocketTransport, since the SDK's *AcpAgentTransport names are for the agent's side of the connection; and AcpAgentSession shares its simple name with the SDK's agent-side com.agentclientprotocol.sdk.agent.AcpAgentSession, a class an application using this library has no reason to import.
  • A standalone configuration file must now be imported with the acp: prefix: spring.config.import: optional:acp:agents.yaml. A bare optional:agents.yaml is no longer claimed by name, because Boot asks this library's resolver before its own, and claiming the name took the file from any other library that reads an agents.yaml. Without the prefix Boot now loads the file as ordinary configuration, so its keys miss spring.acp and are silently ignored: add acp: to the import.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• spring-ai-acp-harness-client-mcp-oauth: a sign-in that had lapsed — its refresh token no longer honoured — was never cleared, so the user was never asked to sign in again and every session after failed to load the server (with goose, "discover and legacy initialize both failed"). The authorization server behind the Tanzu MCP gateway refuses such a refresh with a 401, which Spring Security reads as invalid_token_response instead of invalid_grant; an OAuth error in a 401 from the token endpoint is now read as what it says.
  • spring-ai-acp-harness-client-mcp-oauth: an expired token is now refreshed as the session opens, so a refresh the server refuses leads straight to signing in again (a browser in mode: local, a redirect in mode: web) instead of failing the session's first request. A refresh that fails without a refusal, such as an authorization server that is down, still keeps the token for next time.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• ACP Java SDK 0.18.0, with its Jackson 3 JSON module (acp-json-jackson3). The SDK no longer carries a JSON implementation in acp-core, and this library now uses Jackson 3 throughout, as Spring Boot 4 and Spring AI 2 do. Jackson 2 no longer arrives through Spring AI ACP: an application that used com.fasterxml.jackson.databind without declaring it must now add it itself. Jackson's annotations (com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation) are unchanged.
  • Spring Boot 4.1.1, which brings Jackson 3.1.5, the version the SDK is built against.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• With goose serve, an answer to the agent (a permission decision, a file read, a terminal result) could be dropped when it was sent at the same moment as a new request, leaving that turn waiting until it timed out. The SDK fixed the same race in its own WebSocket transport in 0.18.0.
  • With goose serve, a request in flight when the connection drops now fails at once instead of waiting out the request timeout, so the turn ends with an error straight away.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• auth: provided for an MCP server whose credentials come from the application's own McpCredentialsProvider. Such a server may omit url: the provider supplies the upstream with McpCredentials.routed(url, credentials) when the session opens, as a credential broker that issues a token together with its endpoint does. A URL-less server the provider does not route is left out of that session instead of refusing it.
  • A Tanzu AI Models (GenAI) service bound on Cloud Foundry becomes the provider with no configuration. Its OpenAI-compatible endpoint is used as spring.acp.provider.base-url and api-key, and when no spring.acp.model is set, the first TOOLS-capable model in its catalog is chosen.
  • An explicitly configured provider wins.
  • spring.acp.tanzu-ai.enabled and service-name control it.
  • CODEX_ACP_CLI_PATH names a local codex-acp for the Codex runtime to launch in place of npx, as GOOSE_CLI_PATH and OPENCODE_CLI_PATH do for theirs. The Codex supply buildpack exports it. spring.acp.runtimes.codex.command still wins, and so does an explicit package, which asks for npx.
  • Goose's todo list arrives as AgentEvent.PlanUpdated. Goose keeps its task list in a tool and sends no ACP plan update, so each todo__todo_write call is read as the agent's plan instead of being reported as a tool call. AgentRuntime.planOf is the hook any adapter can use for an agent that does the same.
  • Helpers for runtime adapters, so their shared rules live in core:
  • AgentEnvironment.layered builds a launch environment in the order every adapter uses. Agent defaults come first, then provider credentials, then the tier-3 env block, which wins.
  • Executables.fromEnvironment reads an executable path from an environment variable such as GOOSE_CLI_PATH, and checks it at startup.
  • AgentSettings.findModel() returns the requested model, or empty when it is blank.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • AcpProperties and its nested types are records, bound through their constructors. Code that reads them uses record accessors (properties.model(), properties.pool().sessionTtl()) in place of getters. Property names, defaults and metadata are unchanged, except that spring.acp.protocol.max-version now lists its default (1) in the metadata. A test that declared new AcpProperties() as a bean registers it with @EnableConfigurationProperties(AcpProperties.class) instead.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • OpenCode sessions no longer call MCP servers as another user, or through a closed session's route. OpenCode keeps one MCP client per server name for its whole process, replaced by each session/new, so every session used the route of the one opened last. A runtime now declares this with AgentRuntime.mcpScope() (PROCESS for OpenCode). The pool then keeps each such process to one principal at a time, restarting an idle process before it serves someone else, and McpAccess gives the principal one route shared by all of their sessions, held until the last closes. spring.acp.pool.max-processes caps how many users hold OpenCode sessions at once, and each costs a whole OpenCode process (about 650 MB); see "Processes, users and memory" in the user guide.
Initial release as Spring AI ACP, under the org.springaicommunity groupId and the Apache License 2.0.

docs.title: Agents and runtimes
docs.text:
• AgentClient, a fluent client that drives any Agent Client Protocol v1 coding agent and streams each turn as AgentEvents, with exactly one terminal event per turn.
  • Compiled runtime adapters for Goose, Codex (codex-acp) and OpenCode, selected by spring.acp.runtime, and spring-ai-acp-boot-starter-registry, which launches any agent the ACP registry publishes from a cached catalogue, with SHA-256-verified downloads.
  • A supervised goose serve over WebSocket, as an alternative to stdio.
  • ACP version negotiation; v2 is behind a feature flag and refused.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• Three configuration tiers: portable (spring.acp.*), negotiated (model, mode and provider, resolved against the options the agent advertises, with on-unsupported = fail/warn/ignore), and runtime-specific (spring.acp.runtimes.<id>.*).
  • Bring-your-own OpenAI-compatible endpoints through spring.acp.provider.base-url, with the endpoint's own model listing deciding which models are valid.
  • A standalone agents.yaml, loaded as Spring config data.

docs.title: Sessions, MCP and skills
docs.text:
• Capability-gated session list, load, resume and delete, with connection pooling and idle session sweeping.
  • MCP servers declared per session, with credentials kept out of the agent: HTTP servers that need them are reached through a loopback proxy, one unguessable route per session.
  • spring-ai-acp-mcp-oauth: per-user MCP-spec OAuth, redirecting through Spring Security in a web application or signing in through a loopback browser flow in a terminal one.
  • Detection of MCP servers that goose fails to load, which ACP never reports on the wire, surfaced as AgentClient.notices() and acted on through spring.acp.mcp.on-server-failure.
  • Skills installed from Git (optionally pinned to a commit) into the workspace.

docs.title: Permissions and the workspace
docs.text:
• Permission policies (deny, allowlist, auto-approve and ask), with ask answered by a person through a PermissionPrompt.
  • A workspace jail that confines the agent's filesystem and terminal requests by real path.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
• AcpChatModel, which publishes the agent as a Spring AI ChatModel.
  • An opt-in HTTP endpoint, and the AgentExecutor facade.
  • spring-ai-acp-console, a terminal chat over the application's agent for prototyping it.
  • A Micrometer observation per turn and per tool call, and AgentEvent.UsageUpdated.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: • spring-ai-acp-test: AgentRuntimeContract, the cross-adapter contract test; AgentProbe, which gates live suites on a real session; and ScriptedAgent, a fake agent speaking raw JSON-RPC for wire-format tests. Live-agent suites are opt-in with -Dspring-ai-acp.test.live=true.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 21 or later and Spring Boot 4.1.

  • An agent you can run. Spring AI ACP Harness Client (SAAHC) does not package agent binaries. For the compiled adapters:

    • Goose: the goose CLI on the PATH, or GOOSE_CLI_PATH pointing at it. Verified against goose 1.57.0.
    • Codex: Node.js with npx. The adapter runs npx -y @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@2.5.0, so the first start downloads it. CODEX_ACP_CLI_PATH names a local codex-acp to run instead.
    • OpenCode: the opencode CLI on the PATH, or OPENCODE_CLI_PATH. Verified against opencode 2.2.4.
    • Registry agents: nothing pre-installed; the agent is downloaded and checksum-verified. Agents distributed through npm or PyPI need npx or uvx.

  • Model credentials, either already configured in the agent itself (for example goose configure or codex login) or given to SAAHC through spring.ai.acp.harness.provider (see Models and Providers).

docs.title: Add the dependency
docs.text:
Releases are on Maven Central. Add one runtime starter:

MavenGradle 
<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.springaicommunity</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-goose</artifactId>
        <version>0.7.0</version>
    </dependency>
</dependencies>

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    implementation("org.springaicommunity:spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-goose:0.7.0")
}

Replace -goose with -codex, -opencode or -registry for another agent. No @Enable… annotation or bean definition is needed.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
src/main/resources/application.yaml
spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        runtime: goose                  # optional while goose is the only adapter on the classpath
        workspace: ${AGENT_WORKSPACE:./workspace}   # the agent's working directory; must exist
        timeout: 5m                     # longest a single turn may take

The workspace is the agent's working directory (its ACP session cwd). It is also where the agent looks for AGENTS.md and where skills are installed, so most of this guide comes back to it. A relative path is resolved against the JVM's working directory; left unset, the JVM's working directory itself is used. It must be an existing directory.

docs.title: Send a prompt
docs.text:
@SpringBootApplication
public class ReviewApplication {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(ReviewApplication.class, args);
    }

    @Bean
    ApplicationRunner demo(AcpHarnessClient acpHarnessClient) {
        return args -> System.out.println(
                acpHarnessClient.prompt("Summarize what is in this directory").call().content());
    }
}

AcpHarnessClient is a thread-safe singleton. The agent process is started on the first prompt, not at context refresh: an application whose agent is misconfigured still starts, and reports the problem the first time it is used. The process is stopped when the context closes.

Tip

The repository's samples/smoke-app has all three adapters and the registry on its classpath. After ./mvnw install in the SAAHC checkout, run it against each agent in turn:

./mvnw -pl samples/smoke-app spring-boot:run
./mvnw -pl samples/smoke-app spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.arguments=--spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime=codex
./mvnw -pl samples/smoke-app spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.arguments=--spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime=opencode
./mvnw -pl samples/smoke-app spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.arguments=--spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime=gemini

docs.title: AcpHarnessClient API
docs.text:
Every call starts with prompt() and describes one turn. Nothing is sent until call() or stream().

The API is @NullMarked (JSpecify): a reference is non-null unless it is annotated @Nullable, and the build checks that, so where a method says @Nullable the null is real and where it does not you need no check. An IDE that reads JSpecify annotations shows the same.

docs.title: Blocking and streaming
docs.text:
// Blocking: wait for the finished answer.
AcpHarnessClient.AcpHarnessResponse response = acpHarnessClient.prompt()
        .session("review-123")                          // a named, reusable conversation
        .user("Inspect the pending change")
        .options(o -> o.timeout(Duration.ofMinutes(10)))
        .call();

String text = response.content();                        // assistant text only
AcpSchema.StopReason why = response.completion().reason();

// Streaming: every event as it happens.
Flux<AcpHarnessEvent> events = acpHarnessClient.prompt()
        .session("review-123")
        .user("Now focus on security")
        .stream()
        .events();

// Or just the text, e.g. for a server-sent-events endpoint.
Flux<String> text = acpHarnessClient.prompt("Explain the build").stream().content();
Method Meaning session(name) Runs in a named conversation; repeat calls with the same name keep context. Without it the turn runs in a throwaway session closed when the turn ends. Names match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}. user(text) Appends user text; call more than once to build up a prompt. prompt(text) is shorthand. options(…) Per-turn overrides of timeout, model, mode and provider, as an AcpHarnessOptions or a builder lambda. principal(p) Runs on behalf of a user: their MCP credentials, their session (see per-user OAuth). call() Blocks and returns the finished turn. stream() A Flux ending in exactly one terminal event. Cancelling the subscription cancels the turn on the agent.

A turn that ends early, because its subscription was cancelled or it exceeded timeout, is over for the caller at once. The agent is sent session/cancel, and the session stays busy until the agent answers the cancelled prompt. Goose, Codex and OpenCode answer within a few milliseconds; an agent that never answers is given 5 seconds. What the agent sends in the meantime is dropped rather than delivered to the next turn, and any permission request still open is answered cancelled. A turn started on the same session straight away waits for this, as it would for any turn still running.

Note

Workspace, credentials and MCP servers are not per-request options. They are fixed when the agent process starts, so a per-request override would silently do nothing.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
AcpHarnessEvent is a sealed interface of records, so a switch over it can be exhaustive:

acpHarnessClient.prompt().session("review-123").user("Review the diff").stream().events()
        .doOnNext(event -> {
            switch (event) {
                case AcpHarnessEvent.Text t            -> ui.append(t.text());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.Thought t         -> log.debug("thinking: {}", t.text());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.ToolCallStarted s -> ui.toolStarted(s.id(), s.title(), s.kind());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.ToolCallUpdated u -> ui.toolProgress(u.id(), u.status());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.PlanUpdated p     -> ui.replacePlan(p.entries());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.ConfigChanged c   -> log.info("agent reconfigured: {}", c.options());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.ModeChanged m     -> log.info("mode is now {}", m.modeId());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.UsageUpdated u    -> meter.context(u.contextUsed(), u.contextSize());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.Completed c       -> ui.done(c.reason());
                case AcpHarnessEvent.Failed f          -> ui.error(f.cause());
            }
        })
        .blockLast();
Event Meaning Text Assistant-visible text, as deltas. What content() collects. Thought Reasoning the agent chose to surface. Not part of the answer. ToolCallStarted A tool call began: id, human-readable title, kind. ToolCallUpdated Progress or completion of a call, keyed by the same id. PlanUpdated The agent's current plan. Replaces any earlier plan in the turn. Also sent for an agent that keeps its plan in a tool, such as goose's todo: that tool's calls arrive as PlanUpdated, not as tool calls. ConfigChanged, ModeChanged The agent reconfigured itself mid-turn. UsageUpdated Context window used of its size, cumulative for the session, with cost when the agent reports one. Completed (terminal) The turn reached the agent's own stop condition. Failed (terminal) It did not: error, timeout, lost connection or cancellation.

Every turn emits exactly one terminal event, whatever happens, so a UI can close its progress indicator in one place. event.terminal() tests for either.

docs.title: Named sessions
docs.text:
acpHarnessClient.prompt().session("pr-482").user("What does this PR change?").call();
acpHarnessClient.prompt().session("pr-482").user("Any security concerns in it?").call();   // remembers the first turn

Idle named sessions are closed after spring.ai.acp.harness.pool.session-ttl (60 minutes by default). Scope names to a unit of work, such as a PR, a ticket or a chat, so context does not grow without bound. Only one turn runs in a session at a time: a second waits for the first, for up to its own timeout, holding the thread that started it. A server answering many users should not hold threads that long, so it passes .waitIfBusy(Duration.ZERO) and gets an AcpHarnessSessionBusyException at once instead.

openSession(name) opens a session without spending a turn. It is how to learn what the negotiated tier actually achieved before the first prompt:

import org.springaicommunity.acp.harness.runtime.AcpHarnessRuntime.PortableOption;

SessionConfiguration config = acpHarnessClient.openSession("review-123").configuration();
config.applied(PortableOption.MODEL);          // the model this session is really using, or null
config.unsupported();                          // what was asked for and could not be honoured
config.resolutions().values().forEach(r ->     // requested, applied, and by which mechanism
        log.info("{}: {} -> {} ({})", r.option(), r.requested(), r.applied(), r.mechanism()));

docs.title: Stored conversations
docs.text:
acpHarnessClient.sessions() manages the conversations the agent keeps. Every operation is optional in ACP, and the runtimes implement different subsets, so ask first:

AcpHarnessSessions sessions = acpHarnessClient.sessions();
if (sessions.supports(AcpHarnessSessions.Operation.LIST)) {
    List<StoredSession> stored = sessions.list();
}
if (sessions.supports(AcpHarnessSessions.Operation.LOAD)) {
    sessions.load("review-123", storedId);      // reattach and replay history under this name
}
sessions.close("review-123");                   // always succeeds, told or not
list load resume delete close goose 1.57.0 yes yes no yes yes codex-acp 2.5.0 yes yes yes yes yes opencode 2.2.4 yes yes yes yes yes

An operation the agent does not advertise throws UnsupportedAcpHarnessOperationException naming the ACP method, rather than failing on the wire.

docs.title: Other methods
docs.text:
Method Returns runtimeId() The selected runtime, e.g. "goose". harnessInfo() What the agent called itself during initialize. protocolVersion() The ACP version the connection settled on (always 1 today). notices() What the agent reported outside the protocol, such as an MCP server it could not load (see When a server fails to load). isAlive() Whether the connection is usable. Optimistic: false is never wrong, true may be.

Tip

Migrating from the goose-buildpack java-wrapper? An AcpHarnessExecutor bean offers the old GooseExecutor method signatures and newline-delimited JSON events, with AcpHarnessOptions in place of GooseOptions.

docs.title: Agent Instructions (AGENTS.md)
docs.text:
AGENTS.md is a Markdown file of standing instructions: who the agent is serving, what the project is, its conventions, what it must never do. It is effectively the agent's system prompt. Unlike a skill, which loads on demand, AGENTS.md is in context on every turn.

Agents read it from their working directory. Spring AI ACP Harness Client (SAAHC) does not push instructions over the protocol; it sets the working directory with spring.ai.acp.harness.workspace. So installing instructions means putting AGENTS.md at the workspace root. Goose, Codex and OpenCode all read it there.

workspace/                      ← spring.ai.acp.harness.workspace
├── AGENTS.md                   ← always in context
└── .agents/
    └── skills/                 ← installed by SAAHC; loaded on demand
        └── release-checks/
            └── SKILL.md

docs.title: Writing AGENTS.md
docs.text:
workspace/AGENTS.md
# Orders service assistant

You help the order-management team investigate failed orders. The people you talk to
run operations, not infrastructure: lead with business impact and keep jargon out.

## Tools

- `orders__getOrder`, `orders__listFailures`: read-only, call freely.
- `orders__refund`: moves money. Present the refund and wait for an explicit "yes".

## Conventions

- Cite order ids in every answer.
- Never guess a customer's details; look them up or say you cannot.

Keep it short and about things that apply to every turn. It is paid for on every turn and competes for attention with everything else in context. Anything that starts "when asked to…" belongs in a skill.

docs.title: Option 1: a workspace directory in your project
docs.text:
The simplest approach, used by acp-meridian: keep a workspace/ directory in the repository with AGENTS.md in it, and point at it.

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        workspace: ${WORKSPACE_DIR:./workspace}

The relative path is resolved against the JVM's working directory, so run the application from the project root, or set WORKSPACE_DIR to an absolute path in deployment.

docs.title: Option 2: ship it in the jar and stage it at startup
docs.text:
When the application runs from a jar with a workspace it does not own (a container volume, a temp directory), package AGENTS.md as a resource and copy it into place. The agent is launched on the first prompt, so a component that runs during context startup is always in time:

src/main/java/com/example/orders/agent/InstructionsInstaller.java
@Component
class InstructionsInstaller {

    /** Copies classpath:agent/AGENTS.md to the workspace root before the agent is launched. */
    InstructionsInstaller(AcpHarnessSettings settings,
            @Value("classpath:agent/AGENTS.md") Resource instructions) throws IOException {
        try (InputStream in = instructions.getInputStream()) {
            Files.copy(in, settings.workspace().resolve("AGENTS.md"), StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
        }
    }
}

AcpHarnessSettings is the auto-configured bean carrying the resolved, absolute workspace. The same component is the natural place to render the file from a template if it must vary per deployment.

docs.title: AGENTS.md, skills or prompt?
docs.text:
AGENTS.md Skill Prompt text In context Every turn When its description matches This turn Good for Role, audience, constraints, tool etiquette Multi-step procedures, checklists, scripts The task at hand Cost Every turn: keep it short Only when loaded Per call Configured by <workspace>/AGENTS.md spring.ai.acp.harness.skills .user(…)

Warning

Nothing validates it. A misspelled file name, or a workspace other than the one you think, fails silently: the agent just behaves as if it had no instructions. The ACP runtime '…' selected, workspace … line at INFO names the directory actually used.

Caution

AGENTS.md is an agent convention, not part of ACP. Registry agents may use another name (Gemini CLI reads GEMINI.md; stage the same content under both names). Some agents also merge instruction files from parent directories or the user's home (for example ~/.codex/AGENTS.md), so a workspace inside another project's checkout may pick up that project's instructions too.

docs.title: MCP Servers
docs.text: MCP servers give the agent tools. They are the most portable part of the configuration: ACP passes the list to the agent in session/new, so every compliant agent honours it with no adapter involved. Servers are offered to every session the client opens.

docs.title: Declaring servers
docs.text:
Each server sets either url (HTTP) or command (stdio). Both, or neither, fails at startup.

application.yaml
spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        mcp-servers:
          # Remote server over streamable HTTP.
          - name: inventory
            url: https://mcp.example.com/inventory/mcp
            headers:
              Authorization: "Bearer ${INVENTORY_TOKEN}"

          # Local server the agent launches as a child process.
          - name: filesystem
            command: npx
            args: [ "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/srv/agent-workspace" ]
            env:
              LOG_LEVEL: info
Field Transport Notes name both Required, unique. Tools usually surface prefixed with it. url HTTP HTTPS, or HTTP for localhost/loopback and *.apps.internal. No credentials in the URL. headers HTTP Static headers such as a service token. Validated; never logged. auth HTTP none (default), oauth for per-user sign-in (below), or provided for your own McpCredentialsProvider, which may also supply the URL (url then omitted). command stdio The executable the agent launches. args stdio Arguments, in order. env stdio Environment for the server process.

A Spring AI MCP server of your own is just another HTTP entry. At INFO, Spring AI ACP Harness Client (SAAHC) logs the host and path of each server it offers when a session opens, never its headers.

Important

Declaring a server is not permission to call it. If the agent asks permission before calling a tool, the default policy (deny) refuses it. Configuring MCP servers is two steps: declare them here, then grant them in Permissions.

docs.title: When a server fails to load
docs.text:
An MCP server the agent cannot reach is reported nowhere in ACP: the session opens normally, the model answers, and it simply has no tools. Goose writes the failure only to its own log file, and SAAHC watches that log for agents it started:

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        mcp:
          on-server-failure: fail    # warn (default): log it and carry on; fail: refuse the session
          detect-timeout: 2s         # how long session opening waits for a report (fail only)

acpHarnessClient.notices().forEach(n -> log.warn("{} {}: {}", n.severity(), n.subject(), n.detail()));

Note

Only the Goose adapter can report load failures today. On other runtimes these settings are inert and notices() stays empty; the symptom is the model saying it lacks tools its instructions say it has.

docs.title: Credentials the agent never sees
docs.text:
Static headers are handed to the agent and frozen for the session. For expiring tokens, or tokens that belong to a particular user, contribute an McpCredentialsProvider bean instead:

@Bean
McpCredentialsProvider mcpCredentials(TokenService tokens) {
    return (server, principal) -> server.name().equals("inventory")
            ? McpCredentials.bearer(() -> tokens.currentToken(principal))   // asked per request
            : null;                                                         // as configured
}

Each server the provider answers for is routed through a loopback proxy on 127.0.0.1. The agent is given http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<random-token>/<server>; the proxy adds the headers on every forwarded request (so a token refresh lands between two tool calls) and drops the agent's own Authorization. Each session gets its own unguessable route, released when the session ends. A provider that throws refuses the session before the agent hears of it.

An agent that shares MCP servers across its sessions changes that (AcpHarnessRuntime.mcpScope() returns PROCESS; OpenCode does). Such an agent keeps one client per server name for the whole process, and every session/new replaces it, so all of its sessions call through the route declared last. The client therefore keeps each agent process to one principal at a time and gives that principal a single route, shared by all of their sessions and released when the last of them ends. A process that last served another principal is restarted before it is handed over. spring.ai.acp.harness.pool.max-processes is then the number of users who can hold sessions at once; beyond it a new user's session is refused with a message that says so. See Processes, users and memory for what that costs.

docs.title: URL from the provider
docs.text:
Some servers are only located when their credential is issued: a credential broker answers with a token and the endpoint it is good for. Declare such a server with auth: provided and no url, and return the endpoint with the credential:

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        mcp-servers:
          - name: github
            auth: provided             # credentials, and here the url, come from your McpCredentialsProvider

return (server, principal) -> broker.accessFor(server.name(), principal)       // your own lookup
        .map(grant -> McpCredentials.routed(grant.url(), McpCredentials.bearer(grant::token)));

The upstream is read once, when the session opens, and must be HTTPS (plain HTTP only for loopback and *.apps.internal). A server with no URL of its own that the provider does not route for a session, because the user has not granted access yet, is left out of that session rather than refusing it; the next session asks again. McpCredentials.upstream() also overrides a configured url.

docs.title: Per-user OAuth
docs.text:
For MCP servers that implement the MCP authorization spec, add spring-ai-acp-harness-client-mcp-oauth and mark the server auth: oauth. Authorization-server discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE and the resource parameter are handled for you; each user signs in once per server, and tokens are refreshed as needed. Such a server must have a url: it names the resource whose authorization server the client registers with, and an auth: oauth server declared without one is refused at startup.

pom.xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springaicommunity</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-ai-acp-harness-client-mcp-oauth</artifactId>
    <version>${spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version}</version>
</dependency>
application.yaml
spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        mcp-servers:
          - name: finops-mcp
            url: https://gateway.example.com/finops-mcp/mcp
            auth: oauth
        mcp:
          oauth:
            mode: web                  # web (default) | local
            client-name: Capacity Agent
            store: jdbc                # memory (web default) | jdbc | file (local default)

docs.title: Web applications
docs.text:
Users sign in through Spring Security's redirect. Add the MCP configurer to your filter chain:

@Bean
SecurityFilterChain security(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    return http
            .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth.anyRequest().authenticated())
            .oauth2Login(Customizer.withDefaults())
            .with(McpClientOAuth2Configurer.mcpClientOAuth2(), mcp -> mcp.cimd(false))
            .build();
}

The signed-in user becomes the SessionPrincipal of every prompt described on a request thread. A named session belongs to its principal; another user reusing the name gets SessionOwnershipException. On a reactive stack, pass .principal(SessionPrincipal.of(name)) explicitly. To send a user to sign in before a stream starts, call OAuth2McpCredentialsProvider.requireAuthorized(principal) in the controller. With store: jdbc, registrations and tokens are shared across instances (schema: org/springaicommunity/acp/harness/mcp/oauth/acp-mcp-oauth-schema.sql plus Spring Security's oauth2_authorized_client).

docs.title: Terminal applications
docs.text: mode: local needs no filter chain. The first run opens a browser for each server (a loopback redirect on 127.0.0.1); the operating-system user is the principal, and sign-ins are kept in ~/.config/<spring.application.name>/acp-mcp-oauth.json (mode 600), so later runs refresh silently. A sign-in the server will no longer refresh opens the browser again when the next session opens.

docs.title: Goose and MCP gateways
docs.text: Goose 1.51 opens an HTTP MCP connection with a server/discover probe. Some gateways answer it with an error goose cannot correlate, so goose never falls back to initialize and the server silently never loads. spring.ai.acp.harness.runtimes.goose.mcp.answer-discover: true answers the probe correctly on the gateway's behalf. Enable it only for gateways that need it, and remove it once either side is fixed.

docs.title: Selecting a model
docs.text:
spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        model: gpt-5.6-terra
        on-unsupported: fail       # fail | warn (default) | ignore

spring.ai.acp.harness.model is a request. When a session opens, Spring AI ACP Harness Client (SAAHC) reads the options the agent advertises and matches the request against them, in order: exact id, display name, <provider>/<model>, then a suffix match that must be unique. Only then does it send session/set_config_option. It never sends a value the agent did not advertise, because some agents (goose) accept an unknown model id and fail later, inside the turn.

When nothing matches, on-unsupported decides:

Value Behaviour fail Throws UnsupportedAcpHarnessOptionException when the session opens. Use in production when a wrong model is worse than a failed request. warn Logs once per option per runtime, naming what the agent does offer, and continues on the agent's default. ignore Continues silently. A warn, naming the alternatives
WARN  Runtime 'goose' cannot honor model='gpt-4o-from-2024' (the agent's 'model' option offers
      gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, … (94 in all));
      continuing with the agent's own default.

Tip

Leave model unset to use whatever the agent is already configured with, which is the one model its credentials are sure to reach. To see what an agent offers, set a deliberately wrong model with warn and read the warning, or inspect acpHarnessClient.openSession("probe").configOptions().

Override per turn with .options(o -> o.model("gpt-5.6-sol")). Options are negotiated once per session, and again only when a turn asks for something different. To see what was applied, read openSession(name).configuration() (Named sessions); each option reports a Mechanism: CONFIG_OPTION, ENDPOINT, SESSION_MODE, PROVIDERS_SET, OUT_OF_BAND, UNSUPPORTED or NOT_REQUESTED.

docs.title: Provider credentials
docs.text:
An agent either already has credentials (its own login or config file), or you give it one through spring.ai.acp.harness.provider. The provider block is fixed at process start and never per request.

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        model: gpt-5.6-terra
        provider:
          id: openai                  # negotiated: the provider as the agent names it
          api-type: openai            # the API dialect; also names the env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, …)
          api-key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}  # never logged
          # base-url: …               # only for an endpoint of your own; see below
          # headers: { X-Team: platform }
Property Meaning provider.id Which provider to use, as the agent names it. Negotiated like model; OpenCode takes it as the model prefix. provider.api-type The wire dialect. Its upper-cased form names the environment variables: openai → OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL; azure_openai → AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY. provider.api-key The key. Travels in the agent's environment or config file (as an {env:…} reference where the format allows), or through ACP authenticate for Codex. provider.base-url An endpoint of your own. HTTPS, or HTTP for loopback and .apps.internal only. provider.headers Extra headers for the provider endpoint.

Any variable an adapter derives can be overridden from the runtime's tier-3 env block, which is applied last.

docs.title: Bring your own endpoint
docs.text:
Point the agent at a platform gateway, a proxy, or a model server you run, with four properties and no runtime-specific block:

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        runtime: goose
        model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
        provider:
          id: openai
          api-type: openai
          base-url: https://gateway.example.com/team-x/openai   # "/v1" is added when there is no version segment
          api-key: ${GENAI_API_KEY}

With base-url set, the endpoint's own /models listing decides which models exist, not the agent's built-in catalogue, and the model is applied even though the agent never advertised it (Mechanism.ENDPOINT). An endpoint that publishes no listing refuses nothing. This applies to model only; mode and provider.id are still checked against the agent.

Runtime How the endpoint reaches the agent goose OPENAI_HOST (origin and path prefix, version stripped), plus GOOSE_PROVIDER/GOOSE_MODEL at launch. The wire API is not pinned: goose chooses Responses or Chat Completions per model. codex A [model_providers.<id>] table in config.toml, the key via env_key. opencode An @ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider in opencode.json, keyed acp when id equals api-type, with that vendor's built-in provider disabled so the key cannot leak to it. registry OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY (named from api-type), nothing more.

Important

The endpoint has to speak the agent's dialect. codex-acp 1.12+ supports only the OpenAI Responses API, so a gateway that serves only /chat/completions fails inside Codex's first turn. Goose and OpenCode work with either. When one runtime needs a different endpoint, give it its own profile (Swapping the runtime). To pin goose to one dialect, set OPENAI_BASE_PATH in spring.ai.acp.harness.runtimes.goose.env.

docs.title: Tanzu AI Models on Cloud Foundry
docs.text:
On Cloud Foundry, binding a Tanzu AI Models (GenAI) service is the whole provider configuration. At startup, SAAHC finds the binding in VCAP_SERVICES and uses its OpenAI-compatible endpoint as a bring-your-own endpoint, so every runtime reaches it with no runtime-specific settings.

cf create-service genai tanzu-all-models my-models
cf bind-service my-app my-models
  • The binding sets spring.ai.acp.harness.provider.base-url to its api_base plus the wire format its catalog names (<api_base>/openai, as java-cfenv builds it), and api-key to its key. It sets provider.id and api-type to openai if they are unset. A service whose catalog names another wire format is not used.
  • A binding is recognised by a label starting genai or ai-models, or a genai tag, and needs a credentials.endpoint with api_base and api_key.
  • Without a configured spring.ai.acp.harness.model, the first model the service's catalog (config_url) marks TOOLS-capable is chosen. If the catalog cannot be read, no model is chosen, and a warning says to set one.
  • Your own configuration wins, as a whole. If spring.ai.acp.harness.provider sets a base-url or api-key, the binding is not used, so a key is never paired with another service's endpoint. A blank value (${OPENAI_API_KEY:} with the variable unset) counts as unset, so one application.yaml can serve both a laptop and the platform.
  • A provider id or api-type other than openai also leaves the binding unused.
Property Default Meaning spring.ai.acp.harness.tanzu-ai.enabled true Use a bound Tanzu AI Models service as the provider. spring.ai.acp.harness.tanzu-ai.service-name — Which bound service to use when there are several; the first by default.

Note

With goose-buildpack still supplying the goose binary, set GOOSE_TANZU_GENAI_AUTO_CONFIG=false so the buildpack's own binding logic stays out of the agent's environment.

docs.title: Mode
docs.text:
spring.ai.acp.harness.mode selects the agent's session mode, and is negotiated exactly like model. Its values are the agent's own:

Runtime Default Asks before acting Option id goose auto approve, smart_approve mode (all values) codex agent plan collaboration_mode; sandbox presets are mode (details) opencode build plan mode; custom agents add values (details)

Mode matters for safety: see Permissions. Other agent-specific tuning, such as reasoning effort, belongs in tier 3: spring.ai.acp.harness.runtimes.codex.config-toml.model_reasoning_effort: high.

docs.title: Permission policy
docs.text:
When an agent asks permission to run a tool (session/request_permission), Spring AI ACP Harness Client (SAAHC) answers on your behalf, since a server-side application has no human at the keyboard. Every request gets an answer, so no turn stalls. The exception is ask, for an application someone is sitting at.

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        permissions:
          policy: allowlist          # deny (default) | allowlist | auto-approve | ask
          allowed-tools:
            - developer__text_editor
            - inventory__lookup_part
Policy Behaviour deny Rejects everything. The agent degrades to answering from context. allowlist Approves exactly the named tools (case-insensitive) and rejects the rest, including any request whose tool name cannot be determined. auto-approve Approves everything. Only in a sandbox, or when the gate that matters is elsewhere (see acp-meridian's AGENTS.md). ask Puts each request to a person through the application's PermissionPrompt bean. spring-ai-acp-harness-client-console provides one (see the console); without one, the application fails to start rather than guess. If the turn ends before the person answers, the agent is told cancelled straight away and the thread asking is interrupted; an answer given after that is discarded.

To find the names an agent reports, run once with logging.level.org.springaicommunity.acp.harness: DEBUG and read them off the permission requests.

docs.title: Mode decides whether the question is asked
docs.text:
Warning

policy: deny alone does not stop an agent writing files. In their default modes, Goose, Codex and OpenCode all edit files with their own tools without asking at all. The mode decides whether permission is requested; the policy decides the answer. For a read-only reviewer, set both:

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        mode: plan            # goose: approve
        permissions:
          policy: deny

Codex's read-only mode still writes inside the workspace without asking; use plan.

docs.title: Lending the client's filesystem and terminal
docs.text:
ACP lets an agent borrow the client's file and terminal access. A server-side application rarely needs either, so both are off, and are declared unsupported to the agent:

spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        filesystem:
          enabled: false        # answer fs/read_text_file
          write: false          # also answer fs/write_text_file (implies enabled)
        terminal:
          enabled: false        # answer terminal/*: arbitrary execution as this JVM's user
          allowed-commands: []  # empty allows any; matched by file name
          output-limit: 1MB
          command-timeout: 5m
          max-concurrent: 8

When enabled, every path is confined to the workspace by its real path, with symlinks followed, so neither .. nor a planted symlink escapes. This governs only what the agent asks this client to do. Its own process's file access is the operating system's to restrict: run the agent as a user, or in a container, that can reach only what it should.

docs.title: Where adapters write
docs.text: Adapters write agent config files (config.toml, opencode.json) to spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime-home, never to the workspace. It defaults to a directory under the JVM's temp directory named for the runtime. The only thing SAAHC writes into the workspace is .agents/skills/.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
A skill is a directory holding a SKILL.md: a named, described procedure the agent loads when the task matches its description, optionally with scripts and reference files beside it. Skills are how you teach an agent your procedures (a release checklist, a review rubric, how to send an email) without putting them in every prompt.

ACP says nothing about skills, but Goose, Codex and OpenCode all read them from <workspace>/.agents/skills/<name>/. Spring AI ACP Harness Client installs the skills you configure into that directory before the agent starts, so they are portable across runtimes.

docs.title: Skills bundled with the application
docs.text:
The default way to ship a skill, because it travels with the build that was tested with it. Put it on the classpath:

src/main/resources/
└── skills/
    └── release-checks/
        ├── SKILL.md
        └── scripts/
            └── check_versions.sh
application.yaml
spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        skills:
          - path: skills/release-checks          # classpath directory; installed as "release-checks"

This works from an IDE (target/classes) and from an executable jar. Scripts that start with a shebang are marked executable when copied out of a jar.

docs.title: Skills from a Git repository
docs.text:
spring:
  ai:
    acp:
      harness:
        skills:
          - url: https://github.com/acme/agent-skills
            path: plugins/mailgun/skills/mailgun        # directory inside the repository
            ref: 8ae7aaf85bd1283dedb449d7fdb2192e05e27b5a  # full commit pins it; a branch or tag also works
            sha256: 3f9c…                               # optional: expected SHA-256 of SKILL.md

          - url: https://github.com/acme/private-skills
            path: review-rubric
            token: ${GITHUB_TOKEN}                      # for a private repository
  • Fetched with the system git, so git must be on the PATH. HTTPS only.
  • Without ref, the default branch is used, and the startup log names the commit to pin it to. A 40-character commit is checked against what Git actually resolved.
  • A token reaches only that one git process, as an environment-borne header: never in a URL, an argument, a file or a log line.

docs.title: Skill properties
docs.text: Property Bundled Git Meaning name optional optional Directory to install as. Defaults to the last segment of path, or the repository name. path required optional The skill's directory on the classpath, or inside the repository (default: its root). url — required The repository, over HTTPS, without credentials. Its presence makes the skill a Git skill. ref — optional Commit, branch or tag. token — optional Access token for a private repository. sha256 optional optional Expected SHA-256 of SKILL.md.

docs.title: How installation behaves
docs.text:
• Before first use. Skills are installed when the first agent connection opens, once per JVM for a given workspace and skill list.
  • Fails closed. A skill that cannot be fetched, has no SKILL.md, contains a symbolic link, or fails its digest or pin check stops the agent from starting, rather than letting it start without a capability you rely on.
  • Reconciled. Each installed skill carries a .spring-ai-acp-skill marker. A skill removed from configuration is removed from the workspace at the next start.
  • Your own skills are safe. A directory under .agents/skills/ without the marker is never overwritten or removed; a configured skill with the same name fails instead. You can still author skills by hand directly in <workspace>/.agents/skills/ without configuring them.

docs.title: Writing a skill
docs.text:
skills/release-checks/SKILL.md
---
name: release-checks
description: Verify a release candidate before it is tagged. Use when asked to check,
  validate or sign off a release, RC or version bump.
---

# Release checks

1. Confirm the version in `pom.xml` has no `-SNAPSHOT` suffix.
2. Confirm `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry for this version.
3. Run `scripts/check_versions.sh` and report any dependency whose version changed.

Report each step as PASS or FAIL with one line of evidence. Do not tag anything.

The description is what the agent matches a task against, so write it as when to use this. Name the skill in the prompt ("…using the release-checks skill") when you need deterministic behaviour.

Warning

A skill that runs scripts needs the agent to have a shell tool, and runs that script with the agent's environment, which it inherits from your JVM. On goose that is the developer extension, which goose enables by default; name it in spring.ai.acp.harness.runtimes.goose.builtins to keep it on whatever goose's own config says (Built-in extensions). A secret the script reads (say MAILGUN_API_KEY) must be in your application's environment. The spring.ai.acp.harness.terminal settings do not govern the agent's own shell.

Tip

If the workspace lives in your source tree, add workspace/.agents/ to .gitignore: it is rebuilt from configuration on every start.

docs.title: Example: acp-meridian
docs.text:
acp-meridian is a complete client built on Spring AI ACP Harness Client: a terminal chat application that helps business staff investigate cloud capacity and cost findings, and files service desk tickets for them. It shows every piece of this guide working together. Everything that makes it this agent is configuration:

What Where The agent runtime spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime: goose, or opencode, or the codex profile The model and the endpoint behind it spring.ai.acp.harness.model and spring.ai.acp.harness.provider.* Two MCP servers, with per-user OAuth spring.ai.acp.harness.mcp-servers, spring.ai.acp.harness.mcp.oauth The system prompt workspace/AGENTS.md A skill that sends email spring.ai.acp.harness.skills, fetched from Git into workspace/.agents/skills/ The terminal UI spring-ai-acp-harness-client-console, titled and greeted by spring.ai.acp.harness.console.*

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
acp-meridian/
├── pom.xml
├── .envrc                        # GENAI_API_BASE, GENAI_API_KEY, MAILGUN_API_KEY
├── src/main/java/org/springaicommunity/acp/meridian/
│   └── MeridianApplication.java  # main() and nothing else
├── src/main/resources/application.yaml
└── workspace/                    # spring.ai.acp.harness.workspace
    ├── AGENTS.md                 # the system prompt (checked in)
    └── .agents/skills/mailgun/   # installed at startup (git-ignored)

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
All three runtime starters are on the classpath, so spring.ai.acp.harness.runtime must be set and is the only thing that picks one. spring-ai-acp-harness-client-mcp-oauth signs the user in to the MCP servers, and spring-ai-acp-harness-client-console is the whole user interface.

pom.xml
<properties>
    <java.version>21</java.version>
    <spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version>0.7.0</spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version>
</properties>

<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.springaicommunity</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-goose</artifactId>
        <version>${spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.springaicommunity</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-opencode</artifactId>
        <version>${spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.springaicommunity</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-ai-acp-harness-client-boot-starter-codex</artifactId>
        <version>${spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.springaicommunity</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-ai-acp-harness-client-mcp-oauth</artifactId>
        <version>${spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>org.springaicommunity</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-ai-acp-harness-client-console</artifactId>
        <version>${spring-ai-acp-harness-client.version}</version>
